title: Shortness of Breath
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a child (6 months - 3 years) presenting with acute onset barky cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and respiratory distress, worse at night. Often preceded by viral URI (parainfluenza virus type 1 most common). Croup is inflammation of the larynx and subglottic airway. Westley croup score assesses severity based on stridor, retractions, air entry, cyanosis, and level of consciousness. Classic CXR finding: steeple sign (subglottic narrowing on AP view). Treatment: mild (no stridor at rest) = supportive care, cool mist. Moderate to severe = dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM once ± nebulized racemic epinephrine. Dexamethasone reduces airway edema. Racemic epinephrine is for temporary relief only — observe 2-4 hours after administration for rebound. Hospitalize if requiring racemic epinephrine, stridor at rest, hypoxia, or dehydration. Avoid unnecessary agitation — keep child calm.
chief_complaint: Barky cough, inspiratory stridor, respiratory distress
